summary: The Random class makes random numbers for games and simulations. new Random(42) uses a seed so the results repeat and you can test them.
notes: rand.nextInt(6) returns 0 to 5. rand.nextInt(6) + 1 returns 1 to 6.
rand.nextInt(1, 7) includes 1 and leaves out 7, the same rule as substring().
Collections.shuffle(team, rand) uses the seeded Random so the shuffle repeats too.
pitfall: Writing rand.nextInt(6) for a die gives 0 to 5, so a 6 never appears and 0 does. Add 1.
